newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Canada presents proposal to link with Mercosur.
newsitem.headline: Canada presents proposal to link with Mercosur.

text.p: Canada has presented a proposal to join the Latin American customs union Mercosur as an associate member, Argentina's Foreign Ministry said Tuesday.

Mercosur and Canadian officials meeting in Costa Rica Tuesday agreed to advance negotiations for a so-called "4+1" agreement between the group and Canada, Jorge Campbell, Argentina's undersecretary of trade, said in a statement issued in Buenos Aires.
The Mercosur customs union groups Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
A "4+1" approach was the format for the talks between Mercosur and Chile and Bolivia, which led to those countries' associate memberships of the group.

Campbell said in the statement that Kathryn McCallion, the head of the Canadian delegation in Costa Rica, presented a proposal Tuesday to initiate the negotiations on Canada's Mercosur associate membership.

Canadian and Mercosur under-secretaries of trade are in Costa Rica to take part in talks on hemispheric trade through an American Free Trade Area (AFTA). The heads of state of all countries in the Americas except for Cuba met in Miami in 1994 and agreed on pushing for AFTA by 2005. They are scheduled to meet again in Santiago, Chile, early next year.

In addition to aiming for increased trade between Canada and Mercosur, a deal may serve to "favor" U.S. congressional passage of fast track trade negotiating powers for the U.S. government, the Argentine Foreign Ministry statement said.
The initiative of closer ties between Canada and Mercosur was first taken when AFTA officials met in the Brazilian town of Belo Horizonte in May this year.
